title: Compute the 44-dimensional centre block characteristic polynomial (no κ)
body:
## Summary

An exact finite certificate computes the monic characteristic polynomial of `A_3` on the 44-dimensional `(u,v)=(+1,+1)` space of sign character 7 in sector `c=3`.

```text
x^10 (x^2 - 36) (x^2 - 4)^5
  (x^3 - 12x + 8)^2 (x^3 - 12x - 8)^2 P_+(x) P_-(x)

P_±(x) = x^5 ± 4x^4 - 60x^3 ∓ 176x^2 + 640x ± 768.
```

This answers Open next question 2 of [#7062](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7062). The contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit unpaidmoon for #7062's question and #6965's joint-space definitions, JoyboyBrian for the sign-character handoff, aliromman for #4958/#4720's query and Bell action, and krzysztofwojt and the retained #1719 lineage for the one-slot setting. [Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19693333)

## Evidence

- Before, #7062 computed the adjacent 12-dimensional spaces and left this polynomial open. The new verifier solves the six joint equations on 4,096 ambient indices, constructs 44 signed orbit vectors, checks all 180,224 ambient output coefficients and matches the exact determinant to the displayed product. Substituting sector 1 fails the restriction check.
- Warning-strict normal and optimized checks passed on CPython 3.12.15, macOS arm64, with identical receipts. The direct runs took 0.18 and 0.20 seconds. Both registered checks, metadata and pinned sources passed. Committed bytes, modes and source history passed at `4289b2e2bab3789190413f444b0204bfc58d5a56`. The selected source-binding orientation also passed.

Reproduce from the repository root with the local CPython 3.12 path below or its equivalent.

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/c3-weight3-plus-plus-charpoly/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/c3-weight3-plus-plus-charpoly/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/c3-weight3-plus-plus-charpoly
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/c3-weight3-plus-plus-charpoly --check-source-history
```

Expected markers are `PASS_C3_WEIGHT3_PLUS_PLUS_CHARPOLY`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.

## Limitations

The certificate covers one historical block at one tensor width. The other sign characters and the global stable polynomial remain open in this scope. No predecessor scientific verifier, selected cold replay, Lean or Docker was run. Native caller costs, supplier admission, κ and the multiplication theorem are outside the claim. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

Test whether a signed coordinate symmetry transports this block to each of the other three weight-3 `(+1,+1)` blocks. Start with the sector stabilizer's action on character 7 and the two joint involutions.

## Related open work

- [#7062](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7062) computes the three 12-dimensional slots of character 7 and poses the 44-dimensional question answered here.
- [#7021](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7021) computes a separate weight-4 polynomial in sector 3.
- [#7063](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7063) treats odd-sign modifications on that weight-4 character.
- [#7020](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7020) splits a trivial-character joint space in sector 3 by a payload involution.
- [#7068](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7068) computes the polynomial of an 84-dimensional payload summand of the trivial-character space.
- [#7069](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7069) tracks the payload trace under odd-sign changes on the trivial character.
- [#7172](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7172) treats tensor-width stabilization for the parent centre Gram.

## Merge Danger

Two-way. The change adds one research package, with the query pinned as an input.
